title: húsvét, locsol, szilveszter, újév: Easter and New Year

sections.title: Easter and New Year in Hungary
sections.content: At Easter (*húsvét*) Hungarian boys have a custom: on Easter Monday they visit girls and women and "sprinkle" them (*locsol*) with water or perfume. The girls give them a painted egg (*hímes tojás*) in return. *Szilveszter* is New Year's Eve, 31 December. You know *éjfél* (midnight) from Unit 1: at midnight people wish each other *Boldog új évet!* The wish has the accusative ending again (*új évet*). On *újév*, 1 January, many people eat *lencse* (lentils), which are said to bring money. You know the verb *eszik* from Unit 9, and the accusative *-t* from A1: *lencsét*.

sections.title: Key words
rows: to sprinkle with water or perfume

items.spanish: A lányok hímes tojást adnak a fiúknak.
items.english: The girls give the boys a painted egg.
New Year's Eve is on 31 December.

items.spanish: Magyarországon újév napján sok család lencsét eszik.
items.english: In Hungary many families eat lentils on New Year's Day.

sections.content: The day *szilveszter* is named after a saint called Sylvester, which is also a first name. For the holiday, the word is just the date: 31 December.
